Quick triage notes (initial findings):

1) What I see in the control plane: medsure-claims project was recently created and inherited an org label that maps to the STANDARD tier (org label: medsure-org -> STANDARD). However medsure-prod remains mapped to PREMIUM. There is a label shadowing bug in the label assignment job: when the claims project was onboarded the org-level override was incorrectly applied to the prod project routing table, causing both projects to be evaluated against the lower STANDARD quotas.

2) Effect: medsure-prod suddenly started being rate-limited to STANDARD project quotas while client traffic continued at PREMIUM levels -> 429 spike. Clients immediately retried without exponential backoff which compounded the throttling into a retry storm. 429 responses contain a Retry-After of 30s in some cases, but many SDK clients used by MedSure do jittered fast retries that ignored Retry-After.

Immediate mitigation (recommended, low-risk order):
- Apply an emergency routing patch to pin medsure-prod explicitly to PREMIUM routing (policy roll: pin-project-to-tier medsure-prod PREMIUM). ETA: ~12 minutes to push and warm caches.
- Open temporary quota override on org medsure-org to +50% for the next 2 hours to relieve pressure while routing changes propagate. Requires ops approval.
- Apply a short-lived traffic shaping rule to reject retries that exceed X requests/min per IP with a 429 + Retry-After 60s (reduces amplification) — opt-in for MedSure if they want more conservative behavior.

Actions already in motion: snapshot of current rate-limit configs attached (rate_limit_config_snapshot.csv). I pushed a canary routing change to a single node group; it reduced 429s in that group by ~85% in the test window.

If ops approves, I'll do the full routing pin + temporary org override. After immediate remediation, we should schedule a postmortem and a fix for the label assignment job.

We're seeing the same behavior on our side and have identified a configuration mismatch that is causing MedSure's prod project to evaluate against a lower quota. Ben has a short mitigation plan that we can execute immediately. Proposed immediate actions (what we need from MedSure):

- We will pin medsure-prod to PREMIUM routing and open an org-level temporary capacity increase for 2 hours. This will require a short maintenance window (non-invasive, no restarts). Can you confirm you can tolerate a brief configuration change at 11:00 PST?
- If you prefer, we can also enable a retry-suppression rule on your tenant to reduce amplification; this will introduce controlled 429s but should keep your UX less volatile.

I will coordinate the change and keep you updated every 15 minutes. If you approve the org override, Ben will push the full routing patch.

Subject: Incident summary and next steps — MedSure 429 surge (post-mitigation)

All — final update for the day. Quick executive note and customer-facing summary for records.

Timeline (summary):
- 07:50 PST: Customer reports elevated 429s + timeouts.
- 08:25 PST: Internal triage initiated (H. Schmitt).
- 09:10 PST: Root cause identified — label assignment shadowing caused medsure-prod to evaluate against STANDARD quotas while traffic remained at PREMIUM levels. Retry amplification observed from client SDKs.
- 09:30 PST: Emergency routing pin applied to canary node group; 85% reduction in 429s in canary.
- 10:15 PST: Full routing pin + 2-hour +50% org override applied; customer traffic returned to expected throughput.

Impact: ~53 minutes of elevated error rates for a subset of traffic; user-visible timeouts and retries. No data loss.

Immediate remediation completed: Ben implemented routing pin and org override. Marissa coordinated customer consent for change.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Ben Carter: permanent fix for label assignment job + regression tests (ETA 2 weeks).
- Monica Patel: customer exec readout and credits discussion (ETA 48 hours).
- Marissa Cole: schedule postmortem call with MedSure for Friday 02/06 at 11:00 PST.
- Hannah Schmitt: compile incident brief for execs (attached: exec-summary-429-brief.pdf).

Notes from Ben's analysis: 
> "medsure-claims project label inheritance caused routing table evaluation to default to STANDARD. Pinning project-to-tier and adding regression coverage for label propagation will prevent recurrence"
